plan_reconciliation.reason: Route change for openness. The scaffold reached openness of C\{0} through thm-complex-polynomials-and-rational-functions-are-holomorphic; the authored refutation derives it in one line at step 1.1 from the modulus laws (the ball B(z,|z|/2) misses 0), so that theorem is unused and was dropped and lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws was added for the estimate. def-path-connected and def-polygonal-path-and-polygonal-connectedness were added because [L2] spells out the polygonal -> path-connected -> connected chain the scaffold had folded into thm-path-connected-implies-connected.

Three dependencies the author needed and the scaffold did not anticipate, all in step 1.2's proof that the annulus is a complex domain: def-path-connected supplies the criterion [L4] applied to the explicit radial-and-arc joins, and thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself with cor-complex-differentiability-implies-continuity supply [L7], the continuity of those exp-parametrised paths. The scaffold assumed the annulus was a domain without naming what certifies it.

lem-open-quotient-arcs-in-real-line-mod-integers was needed because step 3.1 refutes the sharpened claim rather than only the endpoint claim: it cites [L7]'s strict bound (every interval of length strictly less than one does embed) to show that length exactly one is precisely where embedding fails. The scaffold planned only the p(0)=p(1) non-injectivity argument.

Two definitional dependencies step 1.1 needs and the scaffold left implicit: def-complex-domain for nonemptiness and openness of U, and def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn to license reading a convex open set as star-shaped about each of its points before the star-shaped Cauchy theorem is applied.

def-complex-primitive added: step 1.1 consumes the primitive's defining properties as [L2] (F holomorphic with F'=f) before the fundamental-theorem step. The scaffold cited the existence result that produces F but not the definition saying what F satisfies.

def-sigma-algebra added: step 2.1 needs closure under countable unions [L3] to know the map S |-> union of D_n over n in S lands in the algebra. The scaffold treated that closure as inherited from the cited theorem instead of as its own edge.

lem-integer-part dropped. The scaffold expected the degree to be extracted from a real number by an integer-part function; the authored definition takes the terminal value of the unique lift, which lies in p^{-1}([0]) = Z by the fibre description in def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers. Integrality is therefore given by the covering, not computed, and no floor function appears.

A definition, so the drift is about what its text actually appeals to. cor-piecewise-c1-paths-have-additive-speed-integral-length was added because the definition asserts the directed segment has length |v-u|, and lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws because the boundedness and diameter claim is discharged inline from the triangle inequality. def-polygonal-path-and-polygonal-connectedness was dropped: the boundary is assembled with the concatenation of def-complex-contours-reversal-concatenation-and-closedness, so polygonal connectedness never enters.

lem-subset-of-countable added: the cocountable case of step 1.2 needs that a subset of an at most countable set is at most countable ([L3]) to conclude that the complement of the union is small. The scaffold anticipated only the countable-union closure.

cor-complex-differentiability-implies-continuity added: step 1.1 must verify the continuity hypothesis of the primitive theorem for F'(z)=z^2, which the holomorphy citation in the scaffold does not itself supply.

lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r added: step 1.2 needs density of the irrationals as well as of Q, to rule out Q being open and being closed. The scaffold planned only the countability route to Borelness.

Three added, all in the refutation's set-up. cor-rn-is-polygonally-connected-and-locally-path-connected gives [L6], connectedness of R^2, which step 1.1 needs to certify C as a complex domain; def-complex-domain [L7] states that criterion; def-complex-primitive [L4] states what the assumed primitive satisfies, which step 2.1 contradicts. The scaffold assumed C's domain-hood without an edge.

prop-standard-circle-loops-have-their-integer-degrees dropped. The scaffold planned to contradict via the degree of the standard loop; the authored refutation instead compares two lifts of that loop directly at step 3.1 -- s composed with omega_1, which is closed, against t |-> m+t, which is not -- and closes by uniqueness of path lifting, so no degree computation is invoked.

Five added, none anticipated. thm-existence-of-complex-line-integrals-on-rectifiable-paths [L1] is what makes F_n(z) exist at all at step 1.1; thm-heine-borel-r, thm-continuous-image-of-a-compact-space-is-compact and thm-compact-subset-is-closed-and-bounded together form [L3], the finite bound M on the modulus of phi composed with gamma that the same step needs and that the scaffold recorded only as 'phi is bounded on the trace'; def-complex-integer-powers is a Statement-level edge for the integer power (zeta-z)^n.

prop-linearity-of-complex-line-integrals dropped: the authored identity is a pure contour computation -- the four boundary edge lists are summed, interior segments cancel by reversal and exterior halves join by concatenation -- so only prop-reversal-and-concatenation-of-complex-line-integrals is used. The integrand is one fixed f throughout, so linearity in the integrand is never invoked.

Two elementary estimates the scaffold named the selection without. lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws gives [L7], the triangle inequality behind the pigeonhole at step 1.1 that one of the four children carries at least a quarter of the parent's integral modulus; lem-geometric-sequence-null gives [L6] for the diameter decay at step 4.1.

thm-recursion added: the disjointification at step 2.1 defines its sequence by recursion, each term from its predecessor, so the recursion theorem [L3] is a real edge. The scaffold described the construction informally and did not name the principle that produces the sequence.

lem-subset-of-countable added: step 1.1 concludes that the family of rational open intervals contained in U is at most countable because it is a subfamily [L2] of a countable family. The scaffold cited only the countability of the full rational-interval family.

def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel added: steps 1.1, 1.4 and 1.5 verify the homomorphism axioms explicitly -- closure of composition, both distributive laws via additivity of f, and that the identity map is R-linear -- so the definition [L3] is load-bearing rather than inherited from the Hom-group edge the scaffold listed.

Three added by the authored estimate. thm-existence-of-complex-line-integrals-on-rectifiable-paths [L5] is what makes F(z) defined at step 1.1; prop-linearity-of-complex-line-integrals and cor-ml-estimate-for-complex-line-integrals combine as [L3] for the difference-quotient bound at step 3.1. The scaffold planned the triangle-integral construction without naming the existence and estimate results it rests on.

thm-omega-one-is-the-least-uncountable-ordinal added: the construction runs through omega_1 stages, and step 1.1 uses the minimality of omega_1 among uncountable ordinals [L6] to obtain omega_1 <= 2^(aleph_0) <= mu. The scaffold used omega_1 as an index without an edge for what characterises it.

Three added for the cardinal arithmetic itself, which the scaffold treated as elementary. thm-hessenberg [L8] carries the product identity used at steps 1.1 and 1.2; thm-well-ordering-theorem and def-cardinal-arithmetic give [L7], the choice scope under which the exponent aleph_0^(aleph_0) and the comparisons at step 1.2 are defined at all.

rem-plane-star-shaped-and-convex-dictionary dropped: step 2.1 proves star-shapedness of the disc about its centre inline in one line, |(1-t)a + t*zeta - a| = t|zeta - a| < R, so the convex/star-shaped dictionary remark is not load-bearing here.

cor-complex-differentiability-implies-continuity added: step 2.1 must know the boundary data f restricted to gamma are continuous before the differentiation lemma applies, and holomorphy alone, which is what the scaffold cited, does not state it.

def-complex-primitive added: step 2.1 makes explicit that the primitive F produced by the preceding result is holomorphic with F'=f, which is the definitional content [L3] that the fundamental-theorem step then consumes.

The scaffold's route -- adjoin generators one at a time and invoke thm-separability-is-transitive -- was replaced by a single separable-degree computation over the tower, so transitivity is unused and six degree-theoretic results are needed instead. thm-finitely-generated-algebraic-extensions-are-finite [L7] makes each finite subextension finite at step 1.2; cor-separable-degree-of-a-simple-extension-counts-distinct-roots [L3] and thm-simple-algebraic-extension-quotient-power-basis-and-degree [L4] give separable degree equal to degree at each tower step at 2.1; thm-multiplicativity-of-separable-degree [L5] and thm-tower-law-for-finite-field-extensions [L6] multiply those equalities, and thm-finite-extension-is-separable-iff-separable-degree-is-full [L8] converts the result back to separability at 3.1.

lem-goursat-four-triangle-boundary-cancellation dropped and prop-reversal-and-concatenation-of-complex-line-integrals added: the authored proof never uses the midpoint four-triangle subdivision. It subdivides at the exceptional point instead -- the three triangles on p at step 4.1 and the two shrinking triangles at 1.2 -- and cancels the new internal edges directly by reversal and concatenation [L2], which also disposes of the degenerate collinear case at 1.1.

Three added, all assumed as background by the scaffold. def-oriented-complex-triangle-and-boundary is a Statement-level edge, since the theorem is stated about the filled triangle of that definition; def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire [L7] supplies the limit form of the derivative that step 1.2 expands into the linear part plus an error term; prop-linearity-of-complex-line-integrals [L6] splits that expansion under the integral at step 2.1.

lem-core-is-largest-normal-subgroup-contained added: step 3.1 runs the action on the three left cosets and needs that the kernel is the core and satisfies K <= H [L13], which is what forces [G:H] to divide [G:K] and hence K = H. The scaffold planned the counting argument and did not anticipate the core step.

Three added for the countability bookkeeping the scaffold did not plan under its power-set injection. def-sigma-algebra [L3] is what puts the union of the chosen D_n back in the algebra at step 2.1; thm-countable-union-of-countable [L6] and def-countable [L5] are used at step 1.1 to assemble an infinite at most countable subfamily from the finite injections chosen by countable choice.

rem-a-monad-is-a-monoid-in-the-endofunctor-category-only-when-that-category-exists dropped: the authored proof states the size condition through def-functor-category [L2] directly -- vertical composition and its associativity in the endofunctor category where that category exists -- so the remark is expository here rather than load-bearing.

thm-finite-field-extensions-are-algebraic added: step 4.1 places every element of L in a finitely generated, hence finite, subextension and then needs finite implies algebraic [L6] to conclude that L/F is algebraic. The scaffold's route stopped at finiteness.

Three real-analysis facts the scaffold recorded only as 'density'. cor-archimedean-reciprocal [L5] supplies the 1/m used to write a half-open box as a countable intersection at step 1.2 and to shrink balls to rational radii at 1.3; cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete with thm-of-archimedean form [L4], which gives the exhaustion of a closed set by its intersections with the boxes [-m,m]^n at step 3.1.

lem-continuity-is-local-and-pastes added: step 1.1 builds the winding map as a composite and needs continuity of composites [L17]. The scaffold listed continuity of sine, cosine and the scaling map but not the closure property that combines them.

lem-rat-embeds-dense [L3] and thm-rationals-countable [L5] added: step 2.1 writes each interval type as a union or intersection indexed by rationals, which needs both density, so that such rationals exist, and countability, so that the result is a countable sigma-algebra operation. The scaffold named the generator equalities without the two facts that make them legitimate.

def-sigma-algebra [L2] and lem-subset-of-countable [L4] added: step 2.1 needs every subset of the index set to be at most countable, as a subset of an at most countable set, and needs closure under countable unions to place the union of the corresponding blocks in the generated sigma-algebra. The scaffold treated both as part of the generation theorem.

Route change in the fixed-point step, plus an existence edge. lem-product-with-normal-subgroup was the scaffold's way to force P = Q from P and Q both lying in the normaliser of Q; the authored step 2.1 instead observes that both are Sylow p-subgroups of N_G(Q), applies Sylow II inside that normaliser and uses normality of Q there, so the product lemma is unused. thm-sylow-first-theorem [L5] was added because step 1.1 must know the Sylow set is nonempty before fixing P, existence the scaffold assumed.

def-comonad added: the whole proof is transport along the opposite category, and [L1] -- a comonad on C is a monad on C^op -- is the fact that licenses applying the monadic result at steps 1.1 and 2.1. The scaffold cited the monad theorem alone.

thm-generated-sigma-algebra-exists-and-is-minimal added: steps 2.1 and 3.1 use both halves of [L4], that the generated sigma-algebra exists and that it is the smallest one containing the generators, to get the two inclusions. The scaffold treated the generated sigma-algebra as given notation.
